title: Anthropic Founders to Keep 50.1% Voting Power on Key Matters After IPO
summary:
Anthropic's seven co-founders would retain majority voting control after its IPO through a new Founder LLC directing a single Class F share with 50.1% of voting power over key corporate matters. The prospectus warns that the structure could produce decisions that conflict with shareholders' financial interests.

A founder would leave the LLC upon quitting, dying, selling too many shares or being fired. Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust would choose four other board seats; its trustees include former Fed Chair Ben Bernanke and national security expert Richard Fontaine.

The governance provisions accompany at least $518 billion in planned cloud, compute and infrastructure spending over a decade. About $413.7 billion, or 80%, is owed regardless of usage, averaging roughly $41 billion a year. Broadcom chip leases, mainly for TPUs, account for the largest single block at $161.2 billion, payable even if the capacity sits idle.

> Broadcom has become the supplier Anthropic would find hardest to replace. Its $161.2 billion of chip leases, mainly for TPUs, is the largest single block, all of it owed regardless of use.

> Anthropic's locked-in cloud payments likely make Google's and Amazon's own AI chips cheaper per unit. Google and Amazon are owed $221 billion regardless of use, much of it for capacity on their TPU and Trainium chips.

> As per the prospectus of the funds, the 7 co-founders keep majority voting control after the IPO.
